grid.definition: The activity with the highest leverage on future earning — the profession being built, the qualification being taken, the venture being started.
A holding that rises with the environment.
The dependable mandate or employment that pays the bills now.
A holding that pays a steady distribution.
Smaller, unrelated earning streams that reduce the variance of the whole.
A holding that peaks in contraction — it pays before the damage, not during it.
What keeps a person functioning so the other three continue: health, network, the activity not done for money.
A holding that pays in crisis — it pays exactly when nothing else does, and costs you something the rest of the time.

levers.note: Erziehungsgutschriften, credited for years with children under 16 in the household.
Betreuungsgutschriften, for years spent caring for a relative.
Splitting, which halves and reassigns income earned during a marriage.
Jugendjahre, contribution years between 18 and 20 that can fill later gaps.
The revaluation factor applied to early-career income before the average is taken.
The reduction for drawing early and the supplement for deferring -- both in Merkblatt 3.04.
The überobligatorisch portion, which for most members is the larger one and is credited and converted at whatever the fund's regulations say.
Salary growth, and any change of pension fund.
Einkäufe — voluntary purchases into the fund, which are the single largest lever a member over 50 has.
A WEF withdrawal already taken, which reduces the balance and the future credits on it.
Risk and administration costs, which are charged alongside the credits and are not part of them.
A part-time pensum changing, which changes the coordinated salary more than proportionally.
Any fund that insures more than the obligatory minimum, which is nearly all of them.

plausibility.ceiling_source: approved by the owner (Nicolas, 29.09.2026, LBS-37), the table unchanged from its proposal in 1.4.0 (LBS-34): the most a portfolio at the risk profile's level can reasonably be planned to earn over the long run, real, a year; 2 % at the cautious end (about the long-run real return of Swiss government bonds), 5 % at the aggressive end (about the long-run real return of Swiss equities), linear in between; a plan that needs more than the long-run return of the asset class it may hold rests on luck

inflation.source: owner's decision (Nicolas, 29.09.2026, LBS-36): 1.0 % a year, the midpoint of the SNB's price-stability range of 0 to 2 % CPI inflation, a forward-looking assumption; it replaces the measured mean of 1.4.0 (0.4997 % a year, 238 months from 2006-01 to 2025-10, datafeed snapshot bloomberg-2026-01-05), which reflects the low-inflation regime of 2006 to 2026

real_view.convention: log returns throughout: real = nominal - ln(1 + inflation); a simple rate converts exactly as (1 + nominal) / (1 + inflation) - 1. A figure is nominal unless its basis says real; the default view is nominal (decision 6)
